def solve_cvrp(instance):
    cust_ids = instance["customer_ids"]
    depot = instance["depot_index"]
    demands = instance["demands"]
    cap = instance["capacity"]
    dm = instance["distance_matrix"]
    nn = instance.get("nearest_neighbors", {})
    hint = instance.get("vehicle_count_hint", len(cust_ids))
    coords = instance.get("coordinates", None)
    desc = instance.get("descriptors", {}) or {}

    # Map customers to consecutive indices in distance matrix space (already are ids).
    n = len(cust_ids)
    if n == 0:
        return [[] for _ in range(0)]

    # Ensure customers are within distance matrix indices.
    # Deterministic: use given ids directly.

    def d(a, b):
        return dm[a][b]

    # Initial: one route per customer
    routes = []
    route_of = {}
    for c in cust_ids:
        r = [c]
        routes.append(r)
        route_of[c] = len(routes) - 1

    def route_load(r):
        s = 0
        for x in r:
            s += demands[x]
        return s

    loads = [demands[c] for c in cust_ids]

    # Savings merge (Clarke-Wright) with deterministic tie-breaking
    depot_savings = []
    for i_idx in range(n):
        i = cust_ids[i_idx]
        for j_idx in range(i_idx + 1, n):
            j = cust_ids[j_idx]
            s = d(depot, i) + d(depot, j) - d(i, j)
            depot_savings.append((s, i, j))
    depot_savings.sort(key=lambda t: (-t[0], t[1], t[2]))

    def can_merge(ri_idx, rj_idx, left_rev, right_rev, i, j):
        # i must be at appropriate end of its route; j must be at appropriate end of its route.
        # We'll only allow end-to-start merges.
        ri = routes[ri_idx]
        rj = routes[rj_idx]
        if left_rev:
            # want i at start
            if not ri or ri[0] != i:
                return False
        else:
            # want i at end
            if not ri or ri[-1] != i:
                return False
        if right_rev:
            # want j at end
            if not rj or rj[-1] != j:
                return False
        else:
            # want j at start
            if not rj or rj[0] != j:
                return False
        # Capacity check after orientation: merge ri + (maybe reversed rj) with i side fixed.
        # left_rev means reverse ri to have i at end; right_rev means reverse rj so j at start.
        new_load = loads[ri_idx] + loads[rj_idx]
        return new_load <= cap

    # We'll perform merge by checking four orientation cases deterministically:
    # end(i) + start(j), end(i) + end(j), start(i) + start(j), start(i) + end(j)
    # but constrained to a final orientation where i is at end of left and j at start of right.
    active = [True] * len(routes)

    def apply_merge(ri_idx, rj_idx, i, j, case):

        nonlocal routes, loads, route_of, active
        ri = routes[ri_idx]
        rj = routes[rj_idx]
        if case == 0:
            left = ri
            right = rj
        elif case == 1:
            left = ri
            right = list(reversed(rj))
        elif case == 2:

            right = rj
